newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close higher, Oct posts new high.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close higher, Oct posts new high.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed stronger and a new contract high was posted in October on commercial demand linked to an expected tightening in fed cattle supplies and higher cash prices the next few weeks, traders said.
October set a new high of 71.775 cents per lb and closed 0.550 higher at 71.725 cents. Other months posted gains of 0.525 to 0.100 cent.
"With the (large cattle) kills we had, we are going to have a fairly tight situation" for fed cattle in the coming weeks, said Karl Skold, Director of Research for Frontier Risk Management.
Skold expects cash cattle prices to move up over futures before peaking during October in the $72 to $73 per cwt area.
R.J. O'Brien bought October and December late while RBH and Rosenthal Collins bought December, traders said. Refco also spread long October/short February early, sources said.
In live cattle options, LIT division of First Options sold February 66 calls and Term Commodities bought. Volatility was weak, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures gained on local and commission house buying linked to higher live cattle futures and mostly lower corn futures. Reduced fed cattle supplies, as indicated by the latest USDA Cattle-on-Feed Report, also indicates good demand for replacement feeders when feed supplies become more abundant with the fall harvest, traders said.
"There are going to be a lot of people willing to pay up for feeders because there is going to be pretty strong demand for them just because the (feed)lots are empty," Skold said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was also up $0.08 to $63.28 per cwt, traders said.
Feeder cattle futures closed unchanged to 0.325 cent higher with October up 0.200 at 63.025 cents a lb.
